arxiv-2101-04058.title: Partitions With Designated Summands Not Divisible by 2 l 2^{l} , 2 2 , and 3 l 3^{l} Modulo 2 2 , 4 4 , and 3 3
arxiv-2101-04058.creator: Daniel Herden, Mark R. Sepanski, Jonathan Stanfill, Cordell Hammon, Joel Henningsen, Henry Ickes, Indalecio Ruiz
arxiv-2101-04058.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniel Herden, Mark R. Sepanski, Jonathan Stanfill, Cordell Hammon, Joel Henningsen, Henry Ickes, Indalecio Ruiz. Numerous congruences for partitions with designated summands have been proven since first being introduced and studied by Andrews, Lewis, and Lovejoy. This paper explicitly characterizes the number of partitions with designated summands whose parts are not divisible by 2 ℓ 2^{\ell} , 2 2 , and 3 ℓ 3^{\ell} working modulo 2 , 4 , 2,\ 4, and 3 3 , respectively, greatly extending previous results on the subject.

arxiv-2205-08413.description: Abstract Many questions in neuroscience involve understanding of the responses of large populations of neurons. However, when dealing with large-scale neural activity, interpretation becomes difficult, and comparisons between two animals, or across different time points becomes challenging. arxiv-2206-10279.title: A complete metric space without non-trivial separable Lipschitz retracts. Thanks: This research was supported by CAAS CZ.02.1.01/0.0/0.0/16-019/0000778 and by the project SGS21/056/OHK3/1T/13. Thanks: The second author’s research has been supported by PAID-01-19
arxiv-2206-10279.creator: Petr Hájek, Andrés Quilis
arxiv-2206-10279.description: Abstract . We construct a complete metric space M M of cardinality continuum such that every non-singleton closed separable subset of M M fails to be a Lipschitz retract of M M . This provides a metric analogue to the various classical and recent examples of Banach spaces failing to have linearly complemented subspaces of prescribed smaller density character.

arxiv-2302-00082.title: Adaptive sparseness for correntropy-based robust regression via automatic relevance determination Thanks: This work was supported in part by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) KAKENHI under Grant 19H05728, in part by the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) Support for the Pi
arxiv-2302-00082.creator: Yuanhao Li*, Badong Chen, Okito Yamashita, Natsue Yoshimura, and Yasuharu Koike
arxiv-2302-00082.description: Abstract Sparseness and robustness are two important properties for many machine learning scenarios. In the present study, regarding the maximum correntropy criterion (MCC) based robust regression algorithm, we investigate to integrate the MCC method with the automatic relevance determination (ARD) technique in a Bayesian framework, so that MCC-based robust regression could be implemented with ‘ adaptive sparseness ’.

arxiv-2302-08381.title: Fast evaluation of spherical harmonics with sphericart
arxiv-2302-08381.creator: Filippo Bigi, Guillaume Fraux, Nicholas J. Browning, Michele Ceriotti
arxiv-2302-08381.description: Abstract Spherical harmonics provide a smooth, orthogonal, and symmetry-adapted basis to expand functions on a sphere, and they are used routinely in physical and theoretical chemistry as well as in different fields of science and technology, from geology and atmospheric sciences to signal processing and computer graphics.

arxiv-2304-14863.title: High-frequency Limits for 3D-Printed Gradient-index (GRIN) Lens Antennas Manuscript received November 22, 2021; accepted December 19, 2022. This work was supported in part by the National Science Foundation under award CNS-1439682-011 (BWAC IUCRC) and the Department of the Navy, Office of Naval Rese
arxiv-2304-14863.creator: Jonathan Chisum
arxiv-2304-14863.description: Abstract Artificial dielectrics are widely used for Gradient-Index (GRIN) lens antennas. The unit-cell size of an artificial dielectric determines the maximum operating frequency and also drives cost and yield. To explore the frequency limitations we printed four identical Luneburg lens antennas using gyroid unit-cells of 12.5, 10, 7.5, and 5 mm and measured their gain over the K- and Ka-band.

arxiv-2505-17335.title: Secure Parsing and Serializing with Separation Logic Applied to CBOR, CDDL, and COSE
arxiv-2505-17335.creator: Tahina Ramananandro, Gabriel Ebner, Guido Martínez, Nikhil Swamy
arxiv-2505-17335.description: Abstract . Incorrect handling of security-critical data formats, particularly in low-level languages, are the root cause of many security vulnerabilities. Provably correct parsing and serialization tools that target languages like C can help. Towards this end, we present PulseParse, a library of verified parser and serializer combinators for non-malleable binary formats.

arxiv-2509-00267.title: Multi-messengers from the radioactive decay of r r -process nuclei
arxiv-2509-00267.creator: Axel Gross, Samuel Cupp, Matthew R. Mumpower
arxiv-2509-00267.description: Abstract The radioactive β \beta -decay of nuclei synthesized in the rapid neutron capture process ( r r -process) releases a variety of particles, including electrons, γ \gamma -rays, neutrinos, and neutrons. These particles provide a rich set of multi-messenger signals that carry information about the astrophysical environments where neutron-rich nucleosynthesis occurs.

arxiv-2511-06091.title: Characterizing AI Manipulation Risks in Brazilian YouTube Climate Discourse
arxiv-2511-06091.creator: Wenchao Dong, Marcelo Sartori Locatelli, Virgilio Almeida, Meeyoung Cha
arxiv-2511-06091.description: Abstract Climate change poses a global threat to public health, food security, and economic stability. Addressing it requires evidence-based policies and a nuanced understanding of how the threat is perceived by the public, particularly within visual social media, where narratives quickly evolve through voices of individuals, politicians, NGOs, and institutions.

arxiv-2602-06467.title: Codes for Metastability-Containing Addition This work has been accepted for publication at IEEE Transactions on Computers. Funding: This research was supported by the Israel Science Foundation under Grants 867/19 and 554/23. This research was funded in part by the French Agence Nationale de la Reche
arxiv-2602-06467.creator: Johannes Bund 1 , and Christoph Lenzen 2 , and Moti Medina 3
arxiv-2602-06467.description: Abstract We investigate the fundamental task of addition under uncertainty, namely, addends that are represented as intervals of numbers rather than single values. One potential source of such uncertainty can occur when obtaining discrete-valued measurements of analog values, which are prone to metastability. Naturally, unstable bits impact gate-level and, consequently, circuit-level computations.

pmc-10624199.title: The Perspective of Patients and Health Professionals on the Prioritization of Assisted Reproductive Techniques. The PRIOFER Study
pmc-10624199.creator: César Lizán Tudela, Irene Cuevas Sáiz, Lorenzo Abad de Velasco, Laura Gregori Navarro, Marta Comellas, Francisco Javier Pérez-Sádaba, Luis Lizán
pmc-10624199.description: PurposeTo determine the perspective of patients and professionals in Assisted Reproduction Units (ARU) on the importance of assisted reproductive techniques (ART) compared to other elective procedures, to highlight the relevance of ART as an elective procedure and the impact of delayed interventions on patients.

pmc-10682142.title: Novel partially cross-linked nanoparticles graft co-polymer as pore former for polyethersulfone membranes for dyes removal
pmc-10682142.creator: Kadhum M Shabeeb, Wallaa A Noori, Ali A Abdulridha, Hasan Sh Majdi, Mohammad N Al-Baiati, Ali A Yahya, Khalid T Rashid, Zoltán Németh, Klara Hernadi, Qusay F Alsalhy
pmc-10682142.description: A newly developed water-soluble polymeric nano-additive termed “partially cross-linked nanoparticles graft copolymer (PCLNPG)" has been successfully synthesized and harnessed as a pore former for modifying a polyethersulfone ultrafiltration membrane for dyes removal. The PCLNPG content was varied in the PES polymeric matrix aiming to scrutinize its impact on membrane surface characteristics, morphological structure, and overall performance.

pmc-11375555.title: Robotic radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer: current trends and controversies
pmc-11375555.creator: Jeeyeon Kim, Ha Kyun Chang, Jiheum Paek, Hyeon Ji Park, Hye Yeon Moon
pmc-11375555.description: Minimally invasive radical hysterectomy (MIRH) is widely performed as a treatment for early-stage cervical cancer. However, in 2018, a randomized controlled trial (RCT) called the Laparoscopic Approach to Cervical Cancer (LACC) trial showed that MIRH had poorer oncologic outcomes compared to laparotomy.

pmc-11507501.title: In Vitro Functional Properties of Rosehips from ‘Aurora’ Edible Garden Rose’s Collection
pmc-11507501.creator: Nemanja Živanović, Biljana Božanić Tanjga, Nataša Simin, Marija Lesjak, Bojana Blagojević, Magdalena Pušić Devai, Mirjana Ljubojević, Tijana Narandžić, Ellen Silva Lago-Vanzela, Paulo César Stringheta
pmc-11507501.description: Although they have been extensively studied in many species of the genus Rosa L., garden roses’ hips have largely been overlooked. To investigate their potential use in the food industry, this study evaluated five cultivars from ‘Aurora’ collection: ‘Purple Aurora’, ‘Berry Bush Aurora’, ‘Aromatic Aurora’, ‘Butterfly Aurora’, and ‘Rugose White Aurora’.

pmc-12551273.title: From eveningness to food addiction: exploring the roles of night eating syndrome and mindful eating
pmc-12551273.creator: Büşra Başar Gökcen
pmc-12551273.description: BackgroundChronotype is a key biopsychosocial factor that regulates individuals’ sleep–wake cycles and daily activities while also shaping their eating behaviors. Eveningness has been associated with maladaptive eating patterns such as food addiction and night eating syndrome, with mindful eating considered a critical factor in these associations.

pmc-12686496.title: ETP-specific-knockout mice reveal endotrophin as a key regulator of kidney fibrosis in ischemia–reperfusion injury models
pmc-12686496.creator: Dae-Seok Kim, Jan-Bernd Funcke, Shiuhwei Chen, Kyounghee Min, Toshiharu Onodera, Min Kim, Qian Lin, Chanmin Joung, Joselin Velasco, Megan Virostek, Katarzyna Walendzik, Chitkale Hiremath, Denise K. Marciano, Philipp E. Scherer
pmc-12686496.description: Endotrophin (ETP), a cleavage product of the C5 domain of collagen VI α3 (COL6A3), plays a crucial role in extracellular matrix remodeling. Previously established Col6a3-knockout mouse models primarily reflect the consequences of COL6A3 loss rather than the specific effects of ETP depletion, making it challenging to directly assess the functions of ETP.

pmc-12738542.title: Identification of bioactive phytoconstituents as promising ABL2 inhibitors using virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulation
pmc-12738542.creator: Afnan Elayyan Mousa Elayyan, Abdelbaset Mohamed Elasbali, Marwah Ayed Meshhin Alanazi, Anas Shamsi, Taj Mohammad
pmc-12738542.description: ABL proto-oncogene 2 (ABL2) is an essential nonreceptor tyrosine kinase that regulates cytoskeletal dynamics, cell adhesion, and migration. ABL2 is dysregulated in multiple cancers and represents a promising therapeutic target. However, currently available tyrosine kinase inhibitors are limited by drug resistance and off-target effects.

pmc-12989012.title: Patterns of failure following stereotactic radiosurgery salvage for recurrent high-grade glioma
pmc-12989012.creator: Shivani Bindal, Brandon Gonzalez, Antonio Dono, Roy Riascos, Jay-Jiguang Zhu, Sigmund Hsu, Nitin Tandon, Angel Blanco, Yoshua Esquenazi, Mark Amsbaugh
pmc-12989012.description: Background and objectivesRe-irradiation with stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is an increasingly used treatment for recurrent high-grade glioma (HGG). We analyzed the patterns of failure after salvage SRS to better identify which patients would most benefit.MethodsWe reviewed all patients who received SRS for recurrent HGG over 12 years at our institution.

pmc-13181888.title: Rapid and reproducible haplotyping of complete mitochondrial genomes using split k-mers
pmc-13181888.creator: Douglas S Stuehler, Liliana M Cano, Michelle Heck
pmc-13181888.description: Accurate phylogenetic analysis of mitochondrial haplotypes underpins a wide spectrum of biological inquiry. While multilocus sequence-based phylogenies are standard, inconsistent gene selection and removal of terminal overhangs during alignment trimming disregard non-coding sequence as well as limit the reproducibility of haplotyping methods.

pmc-13404233.title: A Genome-Wide Association Study Exploring the Genetic Architecture of Eggshell Quality in Chinese Wenshang Barred Chickens
pmc-13404233.creator: Jie Wang, Haixia Han, Jie Liu, Qiuxia Lei, Wei Liu, Yan Sun, Dan Hao, Fuwei Li, Xinxia Wang, Dingguo Cao, Xinhua Zhao, Yan Zhou
pmc-13404233.description: Simple SummaryEggshell quality is one of the most economically important traits in poultry production, as it profoundly affects the production efficiency and economic returns of the laying industry. Previous studies have predominantly focused on commercial chicken lines, whereas the molecular genetic regulatory mechanisms governing eggshell quality remain poorly characterized in Chinese indigenous chickens.

pmc-13492087.title: Exploratory Evaluation of a Medical Student‐Led Health Literacy Program Among High School Students
pmc-13492087.creator: Noah Lee Carey, Isabella Johnson, Allison Ruff, Jonathan F Finks
pmc-13492087.description: BackgroundLow health literacy is a barrier to positive health behaviors and outcomes among adolescents, especially in marginalized communities. Sustained, youth‐centered interventions for high‐risk populations are limited.Contributions to PracticeWe implemented and conducted an exploratory evaluation of a year‐long, medical student‐led program for ninth‐ and tenth‐grade students at two Detroit public high schools.

pmc-13508731.title: Resolving Heterogeneity of Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles Through Solution‐Based Biophysical Analyses
pmc-13508731.creator: Hannah C. Geisler, Hannah C. Safford, Ajay S. Thatte, Marshall S. Padilla, Elisa Battistini, Hannah M. Yamagata, Violet M. Ullman, Alex Chan, Benjamin E. Nachod, Anushka Agrawal, Maxwell B. Watkins, Jesse B. Hopkins, Andrew Tsourkas, Kushol Gupta, Michael J. Mitchell
pmc-13508731.description: Targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNPs) enable cell‐specific nucleic acid delivery through covalent attachment of targeting ligands that drive receptor‐mediated LNP uptake. tLNPs are potentially promising for pregnancy‑associated applications where precise delivery is required to minimize maternal toxicity and protect fetal health. Yet, rational tLNP design is limited by an incomplete understanding of how physicochemical properties influence biological performance.

pmc-13572741.title: A multi-stage prospective study evaluates serum metabolomic signatures for the differential diagnosis and prognostic stratification of PDAC
pmc-13572741.creator: Zhouyu Ning, Ying Zhu, Hui Li, Zhiqiang Meng
pmc-13572741.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Serum metabolomics identifies novel biomarkers for PDAC diagnosis and prognosis.•A specific 4-metabolite panel distinguishes PDAC from chronic pancreatitis.•Combining these four metabolites with CA19-9 achieves a diagnostic AUC of 0.999.•The metabolic signature offers prognostic value independent of clinical stage.Keywords: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, Metabolomics, Biomarkers, Differential diagnosis, Prognosis

Introduction

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy whose global and regional burden continues to increase [[1], [2], [3], [4]].
